digest.component_or_area: pytest timeout budget / CI test harness
propositions: The per-test hang budget was reduced from 300s to 20s in commit 6a5c88027c5, but legitimate tests in the covered CI leg cost 18.7–29.93s measured, placing the budget inside the band of normal costs and causing flaky worker crashes on every run.

pytest-timeout with timeout_method=thread expires tests via os._exit(1) instead of pytest.fail(), killing the xdist worker outright and producing zero 'Failed: Timeout' lines—making the crash indistinguishable from other infrastructure failure in CI logs.

A config-only fix to pyproject.toml is inert on its own patchset Verified gate because GitHub resolves ./ reusable workflows at the caller's trusted-main commit, so the gate executes the stale --timeout=20 flags from main and pytest-timeout precedence CLI > INI silently overrides the patchset's ini bump.

The 20s budget was calibrated to a local unit-tier run without coverage and full-suite contention; coverage alone supplies ~2x cost multiplier and the gating ubuntu-latest+py3.13 leg adds slower cores and 4-way saturation, explaining why the same tests pass locally at 20s but crash in CI.

Dead workers under --dist loadgroup re-dispatch their pending items to respawned workers, causing the same item to be re-run and crash again up to the default restart cap, burning toward the 60-minute job-level timeout and turning a single timeout into a cascading amplification.
